 Is GTA 6 Single-Player Only? Modes Explained
 Understand Grand Theft Auto 6's solo launch, how Jason and Lucia work, and what the lack of multiplayer means before buying.
 Written by Larc Updated Nov 18, 2026 Reading time 4 min Difficulty Beginner 01 Which modes are included at launch? Summary Contents See more GAMES.GG stories on Google
 See GAMES.GG first on Google
 Add us as a preferred source and Google shows you more of our guides when you search.
 Advertisement Yes, Grand Theft Auto 6 is single-player only at launch , with no built-in GTA Online-style multiplayer mode. Jason and Lucia share the lead roles, so scenes featuring both characters can look like a co-op setup. Their partnership belongs to a campaign controlled by one player. If you're deciding whether to buy for the story or for sessions with friends, treat the launch release as a solo purchase.
 Which modes are included at launch?
 Rockstar describes Grand Theft Auto 6 as a single-player experience. The campaign launches on November 19, 2026, and its two-protagonist structure gives you different ways to control the story's leads, not additional player slots.
 Feature Launch status What it means for you 
 Single-player campaign Included Follow Jason and Lucia's story across Leonida. 
 Playable protagonists Two You can play as either lead within the solo campaign. 
 Campaign co-op Not included A friend cannot take over the other protagonist. 
 Local split screen Not included Connecting another controller does not create a two-player campaign. 
 Built-in GTA Online-style mode Not included The launch purchase is not a new multiplayer world. 
 The practical choice is between playing the campaign yourself and waiting for a separately announced online offering. Buying alongside a friend can let you discuss your separate playthroughs, but it does not let you join the same campaign session.

 Find two free unique weapons in the Permit Keys: the Assassin Nipper.38 Pistol and the Smuggler Gorse 425 Shotgun.
 How do Jason and Lucia work without co-op?
 Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos become caught in a criminal conspiracy after a job goes wrong. Their dependence on each other drives the story, while character switching lets one player experience both sides of that partnership.
 Choosing which protagonist to control
 The character selection wheel includes Solo Jason , Solo Lucia , and a dual-protagonist option. These choices determine whether you play with one lead alone or bring the pair together during supported open-world gameplay and missions. Dual-protagonist control is a single-player feature, not a shared-screen mode.
 Jason's background includes military service and criminal activity. Choosing him changes the character you directly control, without requiring another person to manage Lucia.
 Jason Duval, story protagonist
 Taking your partner along
 You can ask the other protagonist to accompany you for activities such as exploration, shopping, gym workouts, and robberies. You do not need to invite a friend before using those companion activities.
 Lucia has spent time in prison and wants to build a better future. Her relationship with Jason is part of the campaign's narrative and optional interactions, so the other lead has a role beyond appearing during major story scenes.
 What happens to GTA Online?
 The existing GTA Online continues to exist. Grand Theft Auto 6's release is not itself an announced replacement date for that game, and Rockstar has not announced when a new Online entry will launch.
 If you're buying specifically for Grand Theft Auto 6 multiplayer at launch , wait for an online release announcement and its access rules before committing. The campaign's launch date does not establish a multiplayer release date or entitlement.
 Does single-player only mean no multiplayer will ever arrive?
 The supported conclusion concerns the launch package. It does not establish that the series will never receive another online game, or that future multiplayer will automatically be included with your campaign purchase. Its price, packaging, and access model remain unannounced.
 Grand Theft Auto V provides historical context: GTA Online arrived around two weeks after its original release. That gap is not a timetable for Grand Theft Auto 6. Planning a group session around the same delay would depend on a date Rockstar has not given.
 Is the campaign a standalone starting point?
 You do not need to finish Grand Theft Auto V first. Grand Theft Auto 6 follows a different central cast in Leonida, moving the story away from Los Santos. You can start with Jason and Lucia without completing the previous game's campaign.
 You also do not need to play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City before Grand Theft Auto 6 . The returning city provides a familiar setting, but this is a modern version within a new story, not a requirement to finish Tommy Vercetti's adventure beforehand.
 Exploring beyond Vice City
 Leonida is a fictional state inspired by Florida, and Vice City is one part of it. The Leonida Keys add coastal islands to the campaign's setting. Exploring with your other protagonist alongside you remains part of your solo playthrough.
 Grassrivers brings wetlands into the same state, alongside other revealed areas such as Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park. The campaign's setting extends beyond urban streets, so buying for single-player does not mean limiting your time to Vice City alone.
 Grassrivers wetlands in Leonida

 What should you check before buying?
 The announced launch platforms are PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, so the console release date should not be treated as a PC availability date.
 Installation also needs its own preparation. Player count describes how you play, not how the game reaches your console.
 warning Boxed copies of Grand Theft Auto 6 contain a download code, not a game disc. You still need to download the game. Use the Grand Theft Auto 6 pre-launch guide to plan your edition choice and installation. Base the purchase on the campaign you want to play, without assigning value to unannounced multiplayer access.
